clue.text: Speed around US city to find stately home

indicators.note: one thing placed around another wraps it, so the first word's letters enclose the second's

explanation.surface: A tourist races around an American city to locate a grand country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand residence, which is the kind of building a stately home is.

clue.text: Poor leper without minister or dealer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round the minister
something in poor shape is damaged, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a minister's degree

explanation.surface: A destitute leper, lacking a clergyman, or some trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: the shuffled letters surround the minister's DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A peddler is a travelling seller, someone who deals in goods.

clue.text: Oslo tour direction's not fixed

indicators.note: a tour wanders about, so these letters travel into a new order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: The route of a sightseeing trip round Norway's capital hasn't been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loose is free or unattached, the opposite of firmly secured.

clue.text: Fanciful image of sweet sound artist

parts.note: a chime is a pleasant ringing tone
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter's dreamy picture of a melodious noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an illusion or wild fancy, from the mythical hybrid monster.

clue.text: Extent to which university students have aspirations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: amount or level, as in 'to some extent'

definitions.text: to which university students have aspirations
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the qualification undergraduates hope to earn

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about how ambitious students are; split it after 'Extent' and both halves describe the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a level or amount and also the academic award a graduate receives.

clue.text: Forehead, I said at first, or another feature

indicators.note: at first puts this piece at the front, ahead of the word it follows in the clue
said means spoken, so the letter is taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: the letter I is pronounced like the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone describing a face points to the forehead, or some other part.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken piece goes before the forehead word, as 'at first' instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is one of the parts of the face, so it is a further facial feature.

clue.text: Exquisite woman in a kind of crèche

indicators.note: in puts the woman inside the other letters
a kind of suggests a variant form, so these letters are rearranged into another version

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A refined lady working at some sort of nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: A crèche is a day nursery for young children.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché means rare, choice and refined, close to exquisite in sense.

clue.text: Slippery vase I've broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: An apologetic admission that a slick vase slipped and smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasive person avoids straight answers, as a slippery character does.

clue.text: Condition in which thermostat (usually) is set

indicators.note: set in means embedded, so the answer sits inside the run of letters

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A heating control is usually set in a given state.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is a state or standing, a sense shared with condition.

clue.text: Maybe cheaper donation makes no difference

definitions.note: a noun phrase defined by a verb phrase; it is what such a tiny amount does

indicators.note: maybe hints at a possible rearrangement, so these letters could be ordered another way

explanation.surface: A smaller gift to charity barely matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an amount so small it is insignificant, having no real effect.

clue.text: Jacket to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a warm synthetic top
second meaning: to swindle someone of their money

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a coat going to the dry cleaner's; 'take to the cleaners' is also slang for cheating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fluffy outdoor garment and also means to overcharge or defraud.

clue.text: Almost turn to new crime to get curry ingredient

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
new signals a fresh arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A villain nearly drifts into fresh offending to obtain a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is the yellow spice used in many curries.

clue.text: Very French: licence for wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A permit that lets the French get away with anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is an old word for sin or offence, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Since king changed, the outcome's revolting

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters take a different order

explanation.surface: A new monarch has brought about a popular uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' tempts as rebellion after a change of king; it means disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sickening is nauseating, the sense of revolting meaning disgusting.

clue.text: Picked replacement piano for wife: it's not good

indicators.note: a replacement swaps one thing in for another, here one letter for one letter

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Choosing a stand-in pianist instead of one's spouse is bad form.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the P of the first word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked means evil or morally bad, the reverse of virtuous.

clue.text: Cupid's heart and soul?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the mortal princess Cupid loved in Roman myth
second meaning: the mind or spirit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' looks like a letter-selection hint for the middle of Cupid, but here it means sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to Cupid's beloved and is also the Greek word for the human spirit.

clue.text: Brown's in Italian city's sun

parts.note: the Tuscan city Siena, here spelt with the doubled n of the pigment named after it
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A brown hue appears in the sunshine of an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is Siena with one n; the wordplay is loose, leaning on the earth pigment that takes its name and its extra n from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Siennas are yellowish or reddish-brown earth colours used by painters.

clue.text: Paints English title on pupil's satchel, originally

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
L, learner, stands for a pupil

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the bag

explanation.surface: A child writes their name in English on a school bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamels are glossy paints that dry to a hard finish.

clue.text: Notes rewritten about rare elk's frame

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first set of letters goes round the second
rewritten means set down again in different form, so these letters are reordered
rare as in unusual, so these letters appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Revised jottings concern the bone structure of an uncommon deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the bony framework of an animal's body.

clue.text: Flying east after Spanish agreement to rest

indicators.note: after places this shuffled piece behind the word for agreement
flying letters are scattered about, so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: After a flight eastward, a Spaniard agrees to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a short period of rest.

clue.text: Level, once he adjusted and engaged student

indicators.note: engaged means taken on or held, so these letters hold the student inside
adjusted means altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L, learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Once he'd calmed down, a tutor took on a pupil on equal terms.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a rank or tier in an organisation.

clue.text: Starting gate

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a gap or way through

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the starting gate of a horse race; split it into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for beginning and as a noun for an aperture or entrance.

clue.text: Pull handle on time

parts.note: a lever is a bar you grip to operate something
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to tug a door handle promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' looks like a physical verb; it is the noun meaning influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is influence or clout, which is what having pull means.

clue.text: Computer nerd and he's hopeless at golf

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who breaks into computer systems
second meaning: a duffer who hacks at the ball

explanation.walkthrough: To hack at golf is to play clumsily, so a poor golfer is also called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a computer intruder and also an incompetent amateur player.

clue.text: Unpleasant person has church's internet address

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
a URL is a web address

explanation.surface: A disagreeable man runs the parish website.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a rude, boorish person.

clue.text: It's not essential entertainment

parts.note: surface reading: an amusement nobody really needs; setter's reading: background music accompanying a play or film, secondary to the main action

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like a dismissal of trivial fun; it describes music that is incidental, meaning subordinate, to a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: This music is written to accompany a play or film rather than to stand alone.

clue.text: Most wise old men are on the square

parts.note: a T-square, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: The wisest elders gather in the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagest is the superlative of sage, meaning wisest.

clue.text: Peacekeepers gulp, going back to disconnect the power

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

explanation.surface: Nervous peacekeepers swallow hard before cutting the electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug is to pull out the plug and so cut off the electrical supply.
